finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement in purge: checkPerm's boolean result is discarded, so any authenticated user (even without the admin permission) can trigger purgeAll(). The sibling handler rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated HTTP request to the purge handler from a user lacking the 'admin' perm

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) obtains the requesting user
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for non-admins but the return value is ignored

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm is a pure lookup that does not write a response or abort; no other middleware exists in the directory (only handlers.go). Contrast with rotateKeys (handlers.go:33), which checks mustPerm's result and returns. Cannot verify whether router-level middleware gates the route, since none is in this codebase.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no middleware in the directory; mustPerm is used only in rotateKeys)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm as a bare statement, discarding its bool result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33-35, which returns on failure. The caveat is that any router-level gating is not visible in this codebase.
